title: Ochsner Health data breach, Nov 19, 2026
disclaimer: Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by Ochsner Health, Orlando Health, any news outlet, government agency, company, or anyone else named.
size_basis: Ochsner is the largest health system in Louisiana, and says letters will go to people whose information is involved. It has not said how many people, so size rests on the organization's reach, not a count.
who_is_affected: People whose information was in the files downloaded from one of two Ochsner employee accounts. Ochsner says it is still working out who, and will send letters. It says patient care and its record systems were not disrupted.

known.text: Ochsner says an unauthorized party accessed two employee accounts in its Microsoft environment on Sept 18 to 21 and downloaded files from one.
Ochsner learned of it on Oct 1, determined on Nov 18 that specific information was accessed, and began notifying people on Nov 19.
The files may include names, demographic information, Social Security numbers and health information.
Ochsner is offering one year of free credit monitoring to people whose Social Security numbers were involved.

not_known.text: How the two accounts were accessed, and who did it.
Whether the group Vortex, which claims about 25,000 files, is behind it.
Whether a ransom was demanded or any data has been published.
